detail.longDescription: I created a file with one line "bug line", initialized git repository and committed change. Then I added the second line "staged" and staged the change. Then I added the third line "unstaged". How to add a commit changing the first line to "bug line changed" so that I still get the second line as staged change and the third line as unstaged change without merge conflicts? EDIT: I wrote this question under the impression that Git isolates and commits individual lines independently. I now understand that Git operates on file snapshots and "hunk" sections, meaning a line cannot easily bypass other uncommitted modifications in the same block. My actual goal was to commit a single urgent line fix immediately, without bundling it into the messy, half-finished edits currently sitting in my staging area and working directory.
